'''Susan Elizabeth, Lady Gibson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE|FRSC}} (née Thomas, 3 November 1960)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Gibson, Prof. Susan Elizabeth | id = U4000527 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.4000527 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is a British research chemist, Professor emerita at Imperial College London and Honorary Fellow of Sidney Sussex College Cambridge.<ref name="Professor Sue Gibson">{{cite web|title=Professor Sue Gibson|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/s.gibson|website=Imperial College London|access-date=9 March 2017}}</ref> Gibson is an expert in [[chemical synthesis]] and [[catalysis]].

== Education ==
Gibson was educated at [[Darwen Vale High School]]{{citation needed|date=February 2018}} and the [[University of Cambridge]] as an undergraduate student of [[Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge]],<ref>{{cite web|title=40 years of women at Sidney|url=https://www.sid.cam.ac.uk/alumni/events/40-years-women-sidney|website=Sidney Sussex College|access-date=9 March 2017}}</ref> where she studied the [[Natural Sciences Tripos]]. She completed postgraduate study at the [[University of Oxford]] as a student of [[New College, Oxford]] where she obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in Chemistry in 1984 for research supervised by [[Stephen G. Davies]].<ref name=dphil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=http://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:3bc11347-fd99-4cdb-8ddd-192318934d5e|title=Transition metal promoted oxidation and reduction reactions|first= Susan Elizabeth|last=Gibson|date=1984|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.351488}}|website=ora.ox.ac.uk|oclc=499841275}} {{free access}}</ref>

== Career and research==
After her DPhil, Gibson spent a year at the [[ETH Zürich]] as a [[post-doctoral researcher]].<ref name="Professor Sue Gibson"/> Her early research focused on using [[transition metal]] chemistry and its applications in organic synthesis.{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}

The Gibson Group's work contributed to areas such as, carbonylation, enzymatic resolution, ligand design, amino acid and peptide synthesis, medicinal chemistry, macrocycle synthesis, asymmetric induction, dendrimer construction, linker technology and multi-component catalysis.

She began her independent research career at the [[University of Warwick]] in 1985 and moved to [[Imperial College London]] in 1990. Between 1998 and 2003 she held the Daniell Chair of Chemistry at [[King's College London]], before returning to [[Imperial College London]] where she held a chair in Chemistry until her retirement in 2019; she was Director of the Graduate School from 2013 until her retirement. She was president of the Organic Division of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] between 2007 and 2010 and chaired the organisation's awards committee from 2011 to 2014.

===Publications===
Sue is the main author on over 140 publications, including a text book that has been translated into French and German.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=55456104500|title=Scopus preview - Scopus - Author details (Thomas, Susan Elizabeth)|website=www.scopus.com|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7201899546|title=Scopus preview - Scopus - Author details (Gibson, Susan E.)|website=www.scopus.com|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref><!-- this selection of publications is a bit random-->



===Honours and awards===
* 1990, [[Meldola Medal]] awarded from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (RSC)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/Archive/Meldola/|title=RSC Awards Archive - Meldola Medal and Prize|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref>
* 1993, [[Zeneca]] Award for Organic Chemistry from [[AstraZeneca]]{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* 1997, Hickinbottom Fellowship from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/HickinbottomAward/PreviousWinners.asp|title=RSC Hickinbottom Award Previous Winners|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2020-01-02}}</ref>
* 1999, [[Novartis]] Chemistry Lectureship{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}
* 2003, Inaugural winner of the Royal Society's [[Rosalind Franklin Award]]. She used the award to fund a series of UK lectureships for internationally renowned female chemists.<ref>{{cite web|title=175 Faces of Chemistry|url=http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/professor-sue-gibson-obe-cchem-frsc|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200617165856/http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/professor-sue-gibson-obe-cchem-frsc/|archivedate=17 June 2020|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|access-date=9 March 2017}}</ref>
* 2013, Gibson was appointed an Officer of the Most Excellent [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) for services to Chemistry and Science Education in the [[2013 New Year Honours]]<ref name=obe>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/higher-education-network/blog/2012/dec/31/new-year-honours-higher-education-2013|website=[[The Guardian]]|title=New Year Honours: higher education|author=Anon|year=2013}}</ref>
